betterAuthSecret.description: Better Auth signing/encryption secret (the BETTER_AUTH_SECRET equivalent).

betterAuthUrl.description: Origin the deployment is served on, e.g. https://portal.example.com — scheme and host only, with no path: the base path is appended in code, and a path here answers every auth request with a 404. Required: left out, Better Auth resolves it from the environment instead, where an unrelated BASE_URL becomes this deployment's auth origin and its only trusted origin.

defaultTenant.description: Tenant serving the addresses that name none of their own: "/" and the sign-in screens, which sit outside the tenant path segment, and a script run with no --tenant. Must name an entry of this document. Left out, those addresses resolve no tenant: "/" answers not-found, and a visitor reaches the sign-in screen by naming a tenant in the URL.

pushMaxConnections.description: Push deliveries in flight at once, and sockets held per push service. One agent serves the whole process, so this bounds the deployment. Defaults to 10.

imageCacheMaxBytes.description: Bytes the resized-image cache may occupy. One cache directory serves every tenant, so the budget is the deployment's.

$global.description: Deployment-wide settings, shared by every tenant because they are bound to the single origin / process.

url.description: Postgres connection URL of this tenant's own database. Every tenant has its own database; isolation is per-database.
Base URL of the AOS instance, e.g. https://erp.example.com/axelor-erp. Unique per tenant in topology A (dedicated AOS); shared across tenants in topology B (AOS multi-tenancy).

aosTenantId.description: AOS-side tenant id — independent of the Goovee tenant id. Set it when this tenant lives on a shared AOS instance with AOS multi-tenancy (topology B): every AOS call then carries X-Tenant-ID with this value. Leave unset for a dedicated AOS instance (topology A).

storage.description: The AOS instance's data.upload.dir base path (created on first connect; back it with a mounted volume so uploads survive). When aosTenantId is set (topology B), goovee reads and writes files under <storage>/<aosTenantId> to match AOP's per-tenant subdirectory; a dedicated instance (topology A) uses this path as-is.

auth.description: AOS credentials: apiKey (AOS 9+, generated in AOS under Preferences → API Keys) or username/password basic auth. apiKey wins when both are set.

webhookSecret.description: Secret AOS uses to sign notification webhooks for this tenant (the NOTIFICATION_WEBHOOK_SECRET equivalent).

live.description: true for live payments; defaults to sandbox.

webhookSecret.description: Stripe webhook signing secret for this tenant's webhook endpoint.

legacyForwardUrl.description: Where to forward Up2Pay IPNs this tenant cannot attribute to a Goovee payment (legacy-ERP invoices, unknown context). Omit to not forward.

beneficiaryName.description: Name of the account a payment is credited to, at most 70 characters — the ISO 20022 limit for a creditor name. The value is sent as it stands, with nothing truncating it on the way out.

certsDir.description: Required. Directory holding this tenant's mTLS client.crt and private-key.pem. Must be distinct per HUB PISP tenant — the certificate is the tenant's bank identity, so there is no shared default. Uniqueness is enforced at config load, not by this schema.

hubpisp.description: Register this tenant's BPCE webhook under the tenant-scoped path /api/tenant/<tenantId>/webhooks/hubpisp/... so the webhook uses this tenant's credentials.

payments.description: Per-tenant merchant accounts. A provider a tenant omits is simply unavailable for that tenant.

maxConnections.description: Connections this tenant's mail account may hold open at once. A mail server limits concurrency per sender, so the ceiling belongs to the account — a Microsoft 365 mailbox allows three. Tenants sharing a mailbox share one pool and one ceiling, so they must agree on this value or the configuration is refused at startup. Defaults to 10.

mattermost.description: The Mattermost host is browser-facing — set it per tenant via publicEnv.GOOVEE_PUBLIC_MATTERMOST_HOST.

issuer.description: Keycloak realm issuer URL, with or without a trailing slash. Each tenant uses its own realm.

oauth.description: Per-tenant OAuth applications. Each provider is registered at startup under the provider id '<provider>-<tenantId>' — register the matching redirect URI (/api/auth/oauth2/callback/<provider>-<tenantId>) with the identity provider. There is no global app: a tenant offers a provider only when it declares it here.

subject.description: mailto: address or https: URL identifying the sender to push services.

webPush.description: Web-push signing identity; the public key lives in publicEnv.GOOVEE_PUBLIC_VAPID_PUBLIC_KEY. The service worker registers per tenant (scope /<tenant>/), so each tenant holds its own push subscription and its own key pair takes effect even on a shared origin.

includeLanguage.description: Also load the base language (e.g. 'en' for 'en-US') in addition to the specific locale. Defaults to false.

uploadRecordRetentionHours.description: How long terminal staged-upload records are kept before the prune sweep deletes them. Defaults to 168 (7 days).

GOOVEE_PUBLIC_HOST.description: Required. Workspace URLs are stored against this host and every absolute link is built from it, so a tenant without one resolves no workspace.

publicEnv.description: Browser-exposed variables for this tenant (declared in full; not inherited from the environment).

title: Goovee configuration
description: The single configuration document for Goovee — a reserved "$global" section (deployment-wide settings) plus one entry per tenant, keyed by the tenant id (the URL path segment: a letter, then letters, digits or hyphens, at most 15 characters, because a Hub PISP payment reference carries the id after a payment context id of up to 19 digits in a field of 35). Set TENANTS_CONFIG_FILE or TENANTS_CONFIG to point at it. Single-tenant is a one-entry document under any id, and that id is the segment every address of the deployment carries. Nothing is inherited: a section a tenant omits is simply off for that tenant, never filled from the environment or another tenant.
